name: Arterial Duct Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Patent Ductus Arteriosus

criteria.description: Presence of a continuous 'machinery' heart murmur best heard at the left upper sternal border
Visualization of persistent ductal flow between the aorta and pulmonary artery on echocardiography
Cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings on chest radiograph
Differential oxygen saturation between upper and lower extremities indicating left-to-right shunting

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of continuous heart murmur plus echocardiographic confirmation of persistent ductal flow
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by echocardiographic imaging; chest X-ray and oxygen saturation differences assist in assessment of hemodynamic significance.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic murmur heard throughout systole and diastole
Due to increased stroke volume from left-to-right shunting

common.notes: Rapid breathing due to pulmonary overcirculation
Common in infants with significant shunting
Due to increased metabolic demand and poor nutrition

occasional.notes: Shortness of breath during activity in older children
Excessive sweating due to increased cardiac workload
Enlarged liver from congestive heart failure

rare.notes: Infection of the ductal tissue or adjacent endocardium
Coughing up blood due to pulmonary vascular complications

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible elevated BNP in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing persistent ductus arteriosus with left-to-right shunt
Chest X-ray demonstrating cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
Doppler ultrasound confirming continuous flow through ductus
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with prematurity and congenital syndromes such as Down syndrome
other: Electrocardiogram may show left atrial enlargement or left ventricular hypertrophy in significant shunts

distinguishingFeatures: Harsh holosystolic murmur rather than continuous murmur
Echocardiography shows septal defect instead of ductal flow
Blood pressure discrepancy between upper and lower limbs

redFlags: Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Endocarditis symptoms such as fever and new murmur changes
references: Moss and Adams' Heart Disease in Infants, Children, and Adolescents, 9th Edition
American Heart Association Guidelines for the Management of Congenital Heart Disease
